decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of NorthStar receipt.
decisions.answer: Match RCPT-NS of EUR 180,000 to INV-26012 / NorthStar Events. Recognise revenue because goods were accepted on 12 February; clear the receivable.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Freedom receipt 1.
decisions.answer: Match RCPT-FF of EUR 142,000 to Freedom Festivals INV-26031. Treat as collection against recognised revenue; EUR 58,000 remains receivable.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Phoenix receipt.
decisions.answer: Match RCPT-PHX of EUR 70,000 to Phoenix INV-26047. Treat as collection against recognised event revenue; EUR 30,000 remains receivable.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Liberty receipt.
decisions.answer: Match RCPT-LIB of EUR 95,000 to Liberty INV-26063. Treat as collection against recognised revenue; EUR 25,000 remains receivable.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Opening receivable receipt.
decisions.answer: Match RCPT-001 of EUR 35,000 to the opening receivable. It is a collection, not current-period revenue.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Finally Single web receipts.
decisions.answer: Match Stripe Finally Single settlement of EUR 250,000 to WEB-FSB. Recognise WEB-FSB revenue of EUR 270,000 based on the CRM delivery status; EUR 20,000 is receivable.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Never Call Back web receipts.
decisions.answer: Match Stripe Never Call Back settlement of EUR 37,000 to WEB-NCB. Recognise WEB-NCB revenue of EUR 90,000 based on the CRM delivery status; EUR 53,000 is gross receivable before R-17.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of New Beginnings deposit.
decisions.answer: Match DEP-NB of EUR 60,000 to New Beginnings September event. Record a customer deposit liability because delivery is 15 September.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Fresh Freedom deposit.
decisions.answer: Match DEP-FF2 of EUR 30,000 to Fresh Freedom September event. Record a customer deposit liability because delivery is 24 September.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Box supplier payment.
decisions.answer: Match SUP-BOX payment of EUR 105,000 to BoxWorks. Apply against the EUR 130,000 purchase invoice; EUR 25,000 remains payable.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Glass supplier payment.
decisions.answer: Match SUP-GLS payment of EUR 92,000 to Glass & Drama. Apply against the EUR 120,000 purchase invoice; EUR 28,000 remains payable.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Print supplier payment.
decisions.answer: Match SUP-PRT payment of EUR 81,000 to Print Again SIA. Apply against the EUR 95,000 purchase invoice; EUR 14,000 remains payable.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Event supplier payment.
decisions.answer: Match SUP-EVT payment of EUR 100,000 to Event Things Europe. EUR 55,000 settles the current EUR 114,000 invoice and EUR 45,000 settles opening payables; EUR 59,000 remains payable.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of January payroll.
decisions.answer: Allocate the combined EUR 231,000 payroll cash payment across January-August as settlement of payroll. Recognise expense when staff worked, not solely when cash was paid.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of February payroll.
decisions.answer: Allocate the combined EUR 231,000 payroll cash payment across January-August as settlement of payroll. Recognise expense when staff worked, not solely when cash was paid.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of March payroll.
decisions.answer: Allocate the combined EUR 231,000 payroll cash payment across January-August as settlement of payroll. Recognise expense when staff worked, not solely when cash was paid.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of April payroll.
decisions.answer: Allocate the combined EUR 231,000 payroll cash payment across January-August as settlement of payroll. Recognise expense when staff worked, not solely when cash was paid.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of May payroll.
decisions.answer: Allocate the combined EUR 231,000 payroll cash payment across January-August as settlement of payroll. Recognise expense when staff worked, not solely when cash was paid.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of June payroll.
decisions.answer: Allocate the combined EUR 231,000 payroll cash payment across January-August as settlement of payroll. Recognise expense when staff worked, not solely when cash was paid.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of July payroll.
decisions.answer: Allocate the combined EUR 231,000 payroll cash payment across January-August as settlement of payroll. Recognise expense when staff worked, not solely when cash was paid.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of August payroll.
decisions.answer: Allocate the combined EUR 231,000 payroll cash payment across January-August as settlement of payroll. Recognise expense when staff worked, not solely when cash was paid.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Rent payments.
decisions.answer: Classify EUR 48,000 rent payment as operating expense.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Meta and influencer payments.
decisions.answer: Classify EUR 55,000 Meta, TikTok and influencer payments as marketing expense.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Software payments.
decisions.answer: Classify EUR 16,000 software subscription payments as operating expense.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Utilities payments.
decisions.answer: Classify EUR 12,000 utilities payments as operating expense.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Repair transfer.
decisions.answer: Classify EUR 10,000 emergency machine work as repair expense because it restored normal output without increasing capacity or useful life.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Packaging machine payment.
decisions.answer: Classify EUR 60,000 Pack-O-Matic payment as a PPE addition.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Photo booth payment.
decisions.answer: Classify EUR 20,000 Regret Photo Booth payment as a PPE addition.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Loan receipt.
decisions.answer: Match LOAN-ADV EUR 50,000 to new bank borrowing, not revenue.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Loan repayments.
decisions.answer: Match PRINCIPAL EUR 19,000 to repayment of bank-loan principal.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Interest payments.
decisions.answer: Match INT EUR 10,000 to interest paid. Total interest expense is EUR 12,000, leaving EUR 2,000 payable.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Villa deposit.
decisions.answer: Match VILLA EUR 70,000 to the owner's personal villa reservation. Treat as an owner distribution.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Owner card spending.
decisions.answer: Match OWNERCARD EUR 40,000 to personal owner-card spending. Treat as an owner distribution.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Insurance movement.
decisions.answer: No insurance cash movement, invoice, or balance is present in the supplied evidence. Do not record insurance expense or a prepaid insurance balance; flag the source gap.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Water-damaged stock.
decisions.answer: Identify basement premium stock at EUR 22,000 as water-damaged and unsaleable. Write it down to nil; disclose the EUR 2,000 disposal quote without creating an unsupported closing provision.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Customer insolvency.
decisions.answer: Identify R-17 EUR 18,000 as a customer in liquidation with no recovery expected. Write off the receivable.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Former employee claim.
decisions.answer: Identify former employee claim as probable at 31 August with best estimate EUR 25,000. Recognise a provision.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Purchase total.
decisions.answer: Use total purchases of EUR 459,000, supported by supplier invoices and confirmed goods received.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Cash collections total.
decisions.answer: Cash collections total EUR 899,000: opening receivable EUR 35,000, recognised sales collections EUR 774,000, and September deposits EUR 90,000.

decisions.question: Resolve the source and treatment of Closing bank balance.
decisions.answer: Closing bank balance is EUR 60,000 and agrees to the final bank statement balance.

decisions.question: Classify September customer deposits.
decisions.answer: Classify EUR 90,000 September deposits as contract liabilities, not August revenue.
decisions.aiProposal: Treat deposits as deferred revenue because no delivery occurred by 31 August.
decisions.independentChallenge: A cash receipt could be revenue only if the performance obligation had been satisfied. Both delivery dates are in September.
decisions.studentReasoning: The signed documents state 15 and 24 September delivery. Therefore no revenue was earned by 31 August.

decisions.question: Classify New bank borrowing.
decisions.answer: Classify EUR 50,000 new bank receipt as a loan liability, not income.
decisions.aiProposal: Record the bank advance as debt.
decisions.independentChallenge: Management labelled it strategic income, but the bank agreement requires repayment.
decisions.studentReasoning: The signed bank evidence is stronger than the management label, so the amount is financing.

decisions.question: Classify Packaging machine.
decisions.answer: Capitalise the EUR 60,000 Pack-O-Matic 9000 as PPE.
decisions.aiProposal: Capitalise the machine because it is available for use and creates a long-term resource.
decisions.independentChallenge: Management labelled it a repair, but the document describes a new packaging machine.
decisions.studentReasoning: The machine is a distinct productive asset, not maintenance of an existing asset.

decisions.question: Classify Photo booth.
decisions.answer: Capitalise the EUR 20,000 Regret Photo Booth as PPE.
decisions.aiProposal: Capitalise the photo booth as equipment available for use.
decisions.independentChallenge: Management called it marketing expense, so its business use and useful life should be confirmed.
decisions.studentReasoning: The invoice calls it equipment and says it was available for use. Capitalisation is the better supported treatment.

decisions.question: Classify Machine belt and calibration.
decisions.answer: Expense EUR 10,000 machine belt, cleaning and calibration as repairs.
decisions.aiProposal: Expense the repair because it restores normal output.
decisions.independentChallenge: Management capitalised the amount, but the repair did not increase capacity or extend useful life.
decisions.studentReasoning: The evidence directly states that normal condition only was restored.

decisions.question: Classify Owner villa deposit.
decisions.answer: Classify the EUR 70,000 villa payment as an owner distribution.
decisions.aiProposal: Treat the payment as a distribution rather than marketing or payroll.
decisions.independentChallenge: The founder described customer research, but the villa is in the founder's personal name and no customer meeting occurred.
decisions.studentReasoning: There is no business purpose supported by evidence. The debit reduces equity, not profit.

decisions.question: Classify Owner card spending.
decisions.answer: Classify EUR 40,000 owner-card spending as an owner distribution.
decisions.aiProposal: Treat owner-card spending as a distribution.
decisions.independentChallenge: Management re-labelled it as a bonus, but no employment approval exists.
decisions.studentReasoning: The cash flow and owner-card evidence support an equity distribution, not payroll expense.

decisions.question: Classify Physical product materials consumed.
decisions.answer: Classify EUR 405,000 of physical materials consumed as cost of sales.
decisions.aiProposal: Use physical consumption on valid delivered sales as COGS.
decisions.independentChallenge: The physical count creates a EUR 9,000 difference from the book roll-forward.
decisions.studentReasoning: Use the warehouse consumption evidence but disclose the EUR 9,000 reconciliation gap for investigation.

decisions.question: Classify Event staff payroll.
decisions.answer: Classify EUR 80,000 event-delivery staff cost as direct payroll within operating expenses.
decisions.aiProposal: Recognise event-delivery staff cost in payroll expense.
decisions.independentChallenge: It could be presented in cost of sales because staff work directly on paid events.
decisions.studentReasoning: For the adopted P&L it remains in total payroll expense; presentation does not change total profit.

decisions.question: Classify Sales team payroll.
decisions.answer: Classify EUR 72,000 sales and partnerships payroll as payroll operating expense.

decisions.question: Classify Office payroll.
decisions.answer: Classify EUR 96,000 office and finance payroll as payroll operating expense.

decisions.question: Classify Rent.
decisions.answer: Classify EUR 48,000 rent as operating expense.

decisions.question: Classify Marketing.
decisions.answer: Classify EUR 55,000 Meta, TikTok and influencer spend as marketing expense.

decisions.question: Classify Software.
decisions.answer: Classify EUR 16,000 software subscriptions as operating expense.

decisions.question: Classify Utilities.
decisions.answer: Classify EUR 12,000 utilities as operating expense.

decisions.question: Classify Depreciation.
decisions.answer: Recognise EUR 24,000 depreciation expense for the period.
decisions.aiProposal: Record the independent depreciation schedule estimate.
decisions.independentChallenge: Management recorded zero depreciation; useful-life detail is limited.
decisions.studentReasoning: The independent schedule gives EUR 24,000 and PPE was available for use. Recognition is required despite incomplete detail.

decisions.question: Classify Bad receivable.
decisions.answer: Write off EUR 18,000 R-17 receivable as bad debt.
decisions.aiProposal: Recognise a bad-debt expense and reduce receivables.
decisions.independentChallenge: The liquidator notice arrived after year end, but could still be a non-adjusting event.
decisions.studentReasoning: The notice confirms liquidation and no recovery for a balance that existed at 31 August, so it is adjusting evidence.

decisions.question: Classify Damaged stock.
decisions.answer: Write down water-damaged stock by EUR 22,000 to nil.
decisions.aiProposal: Inventory exists physically but has no saleable value, so write it down.
decisions.independentChallenge: Physical existence could support retaining cost, but recoverable value is nil.
decisions.studentReasoning: The warehouse evidence supports the EUR 22,000 write-down. The EUR 2,000 disposal quote is disclosed, but no closing obligation is recorded without evidence it existed at 31 August.

decisions.question: Classify Probable legal claim.
decisions.answer: Recognise a EUR 25,000 legal provision for the former employee claim.
decisions.aiProposal: Use the lawyer's best estimate for a probable claim.
decisions.independentChallenge: The possible range is EUR 20,000-30,000 and no cash had been paid.
decisions.studentReasoning: A past event and probable obligation existed at reporting date. EUR 25,000 is the best estimate; disclose the range.

decisions.question: Classify Insurance consumed.
decisions.answer: No insurance was evidenced. Classify insurance consumed as EUR 0 and flag it as missing source evidence rather than inventing a value.

decisions.question: Classify Unpaid interest.
decisions.answer: Classify EUR 2,000 as accrued interest payable: EUR 12,000 expense less EUR 10,000 paid.

decisions.question: Classify Unpaid payroll.
decisions.answer: Classify EUR 32,000 as accrued payroll payable: opening EUR 15,000 plus EUR 248,000 expense less EUR 231,000 cash paid.

decisions.question: Classify Unpaid suppliers.
decisions.answer: Classify EUR 126,000 as trade payables: opening EUR 45,000 plus purchases EUR 459,000 less supplier payments EUR 378,000.

decisions.question: Classify Delivered NorthStar contract.
decisions.answer: Recognise NorthStar contract revenue of EUR 180,000.
decisions.aiProposal: Recognise revenue at customer acceptance on 12 February.
decisions.independentChallenge: CRM naming differs from bank name, but the amount, date, and abbreviated name match.
decisions.studentReasoning: The signed acceptance and matching N STAR receipt provide sufficient evidence that the performance obligation was fulfilled.

decisions.question: Classify Delivered Freedom contract.
decisions.answer: Recognise Freedom contract revenue of EUR 200,000.
decisions.aiProposal: Recognise revenue on acceptance on 18 March.
decisions.independentChallenge: Only EUR 142,000 was collected, but cash collection is not the revenue criterion.
decisions.studentReasoning: The accepted contract establishes revenue; the unpaid EUR 58,000 remains a receivable.

decisions.question: Classify Completed Phoenix event.
decisions.answer: Recognise Phoenix completed event revenue of EUR 100,000.
decisions.aiProposal: Recognise revenue upon completion and customer email acceptance on 29 April.
decisions.independentChallenge: Final acceptance is an email rather than a formal signed document.
decisions.studentReasoning: The customer acceptance email is sufficient evidence of completed service.

decisions.question: Classify Delivered Liberty order.
decisions.answer: Recognise Liberty delivered order revenue of EUR 120,000.
decisions.aiProposal: Recognise revenue on delivery and customer acceptance on 20 June.
decisions.independentChallenge: EUR 25,000 remains unpaid, but the delivery is accepted.
decisions.studentReasoning: Accepted delivery satisfies the revenue criterion; the unpaid balance remains receivable.

decisions.question: Classify Undelivered September events.
decisions.answer: Keep the undelivered September events as EUR 90,000 contract liabilities.
decisions.aiProposal: Do not recognise revenue before delivery.
decisions.independentChallenge: Management wanted to record deposits as August sales because cash was received.
decisions.studentReasoning: Delivery dates are after 31 August, so the performance obligations were unsatisfied at reporting date.

decisions.question: Classify Loan principal payment.
decisions.answer: Classify EUR 19,000 loan principal payment as financing outflow and reduction of bank-loan liability.

decisions.question: Classify Equipment purchase.
decisions.answer: Classify EUR 80,000 equipment purchases as investing cash outflows and PPE additions.

decisions.question: Estimate Closing bad-debt allowance/write-off and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Estimate closing bad-debt write-off at EUR 18,000 for R-17.
decisions.aiProposal: Write off the full R-17 balance because no distribution is expected.
decisions.independentChallenge: The notice is after reporting date, so verify whether it confirms a pre-existing condition.
decisions.studentReasoning: It confirms that liquidation and no-recovery condition existed at 31 August; use full EUR 18,000.

decisions.question: Estimate Damaged inventory write-off and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Estimate the damaged-inventory write-off at EUR 22,000.
decisions.aiProposal: Reduce damaged stock to nil; disclose the disposal quote separately.
decisions.independentChallenge: The stock is physically present, but recoverable value could be assessed differently.
decisions.studentReasoning: Independent stock evidence says it is unsaleable. The EUR 2,000 quote is not recorded as a closing provision without evidence of a present obligation.

decisions.question: Estimate Legal provision and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Estimate the legal provision at EUR 25,000.
decisions.aiProposal: Use the lawyer's best estimate within the stated range.
decisions.independentChallenge: The range is EUR 20,000-30,000 and outcome is not certain.
decisions.studentReasoning: The claim is probable and reliably estimable. Use EUR 25,000 and disclose a EUR 5,000 sensitivity.

decisions.question: Estimate Period depreciation and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Estimate period depreciation at EUR 24,000.
decisions.aiProposal: Use the independent schedule estimate of EUR 24,000.
decisions.independentChallenge: The underlying detailed useful-life schedule is not supplied.
decisions.studentReasoning: The independent schedule is more reliable than management's zero balance; record the estimate and disclose the limitation.

decisions.question: Estimate Closing inventory and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Select count-based closing inventory of EUR 121,000 and disclose the EUR 9,000 unresolved difference.
decisions.aiProposal: Use direct physical count evidence at reporting date.
decisions.independentChallenge: The inventory flow after the EUR 22,000 write-down gives EUR 112,000, which differs from the EUR 121,000 count basis.
decisions.studentReasoning: The physical count is direct reporting-date evidence. Use EUR 121,000, do not manufacture a balancing entry, and keep the EUR 9,000 issue visible.

decisions.question: Estimate Closing receivables and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Estimate closing net receivables at EUR 168,000: EUR 35,000 opening plus EUR 960,000 revenue less EUR 809,000 collections less EUR 18,000 write-off.

decisions.question: Estimate Repair versus improvement amount and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Estimate repair versus improvement as EUR 10,000 repair expense and EUR 80,000 equipment additions.

decisions.question: Estimate Insurance expense and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Estimate insurance expense at EUR 0 because no insurance movement or supporting evidence was provided. Flag the source gap.

decisions.question: Estimate Interest payable and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Estimate interest payable at EUR 2,000.

decisions.question: Estimate Accrued payroll and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Estimate accrued payroll at EUR 32,000.

decisions.question: Estimate Customer deposit liability and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Estimate customer deposit liability at EUR 90,000.

decisions.question: Estimate PPE closing cost and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Estimate closing PPE cost at EUR 260,000: opening EUR 180,000 plus EUR 80,000 additions.

decisions.question: Estimate Accumulated depreciation and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Estimate accumulated depreciation at EUR 69,000: opening EUR 45,000 plus EUR 24,000 period depreciation.

decisions.question: Estimate Supplier payable and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Estimate supplier payable at EUR 126,000.

decisions.question: Estimate Closing loan and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Estimate closing loan at EUR 131,000.

decisions.question: Estimate Physical COGS and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Estimate physical COGS at EUR 405,000, based on warehouse-confirmed materials consumed on valid delivered sales.

decisions.question: Estimate Service direct payroll and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Estimate service direct payroll at EUR 80,000 for event-delivery staff. It is included in total payroll expense of EUR 248,000.

decisions.question: Estimate Owner distributions and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Estimate owner distributions at EUR 110,000: villa EUR 70,000 plus owner card EUR 40,000.

decisions.question: Estimate Net profit and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Estimate reconstructed profit at EUR 65,000 using the corrected P&L and excluding insurance because no insurance evidence was supplied.

decisions.question: Estimate Closing cash and document the basis.
decisions.answer: Estimate closing cash at EUR 60,000, agreeing to both the bank statement and the cash-flow roll-forward.

decisions.question: Approve corrected accounts before valuation
decisions.answer: Approve corrected accounts before any valuation or earn-out discussion.
decisions.aiProposal: Do not approve valuation using unreconciled management results.
decisions.independentChallenge: The management P&L reports EUR 312,000 profit, but bank and external evidence contradict key classifications.
decisions.studentReasoning: Valuation should use corrected, reconciling accounts and disclose the web-revenue and inventory uncertainties.

decisions.question: Freeze owner-card access
decisions.answer: Freeze owner-card access immediately and investigate recovery of EUR 110,000 of owner distributions.

decisions.question: Move September deposits to contract liabilities
decisions.answer: Transfer September deposits of EUR 90,000 to contract liabilities and release revenue only after delivery.

decisions.question: Begin weekly 13-week cash forecast
decisions.answer: Start a weekly 13-week cash forecast with bank, payables, payroll, and deposit reconciliations.

decisions.question: Stop credit sales to insolvent/high-risk customers
decisions.answer: Stop new credit sales to insolvent or high-risk customers until credit approval and collection controls are operating.

decisions.question: Dispose of damaged stock
decisions.answer: Dispose of damaged stock and settle the EUR 2,000 disposal obligation after the physical recount.

decisions.question: Investigate management override and duplicate sources
decisions.answer: Investigate management overrides, unreliable classifications, and duplicate/conflicting source data; preserve evidence and document changes.

decisions.question: Renegotiate supplier terms
decisions.answer: Renegotiate supplier terms for EUR 126,000 closing trade payables and establish a payment plan.

decisions.question: Continue core Finally Single and event operations
decisions.answer: Continue core Finally Single and event operations only with controlled turnaround measures, cash forecasting, and evidence-based reporting.

decisions.question: Use claimed management profit for earn-out
decisions.answer: Reject the claimed management profit of EUR 312,000 for any earn-out or valuation purpose.
decisions.aiProposal: Use management profit only if it reconciles to evidence.
decisions.independentChallenge: The claimed figure includes September deposits as sales, bank borrowing as income, and incomplete expenses.
decisions.studentReasoning: The figure is explicitly unreconciled and contradicted by stronger evidence. Use reconstructed profit of EUR 65,000, with stated uncertainties.

equityAndDistributions.openingEquity: Incomplete evidence; no balancing plug used.

reconciliations.name: Balance sheet
reconciliations.calculation: Assets EUR 540,000 = liabilities EUR 406,000 + implied net assets/equity EUR 134,000

reconciliations.name: Cash
reconciliations.calculation: Opening EUR 80,000 + operating EUR 139,000 - investing EUR 80,000 - financing EUR 79,000 = closing EUR 60,000

reconciliations.name: Inventory
reconciliations.calculation: Flow before write-down is EUR 134,000; selected physical-count basis is EUR 121,000; EUR 9,000 remains visibly unresolved against the post-write-down flow.

reconciliations.name: PPE
reconciliations.calculation: Cost EUR 260,000 less accumulated depreciation EUR 69,000 = net EUR 191,000

reconciliations.name: Debt and interest
reconciliations.calculation: Debt EUR 100,000 + EUR 50,000 - EUR 19,000 = EUR 131,000; interest EUR 12,000 - EUR 10,000 = EUR 2,000 payable

reconciliations.name: Equity
reconciliations.calculation: Implied equity is EUR 134,000. Opening-equity evidence is incomplete and no unsupported balancing plug is manufactured.

uncertainties.issue: Web revenue of EUR 360,000 is supported by CRM delivery status but lacks individual customer acceptances.
uncertainties.alternative: Do not recognise web revenue; profit becomes a EUR 297,000 loss.

uncertainties.issue: Physical saleable inventory of EUR 121,000 does not reconcile to the inventory flow after the EUR 22,000 write-down.
uncertainties.reportedTreatment: Use direct physical-count basis of EUR 121,000 and keep EUR 9,000 visibly unresolved.
uncertainties.alternative: Obtain a recount and investigate the source records; do not manufacture a balancing entry.
Profit and equity could vary by EUR 5,000.

uncertainties.issue: No insurance transaction or balance was supplied although the template requests an insurance decision.
uncertainties.reportedTreatment: Record EUR 0 and disclose missing evidence.
uncertainties.alternative: Update only when a source document is provided.

boardRecommendation.recommendation: Continue the core business only under a controlled turnaround and after approval of the evidence-led reconstructed accounts.
immediateActions: Freeze owner-card access and investigate recovery of EUR 110,000.
Implement a 13-week cash forecast and weekly bank, payroll, and supplier reconciliations.
Hold EUR 90,000 September deposits as contract liabilities until delivery.
Collect outstanding trade receivables and restrict credit to high-risk customers.
Recount inventory, investigate the EUR 9,000 difference, and dispose of damaged stock.
